## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey or peer-reviewed study of the bottom was found.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |

| Swell size | Low | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 1 disagrees. |

| Wind | High | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> 8 sources: 7 read directly, plus SurferToday kept as web_search (403). 7 publishers. Swell direction: Surf-Forecast NNW (337.5); Surf Atlas 'north swell is a must, add some west'; Matosurf N to NW. All fit the 300-345 optimum and 280-30 window. Wind: Surf-Forecast SE (135, offshore), Surf Atlas offshore S or SW (202.5), Matosurf southerly offshore (180). SurferToday (unread) gives S and SE. The profile's 170 is within 35 deg of all of them; together they span SE to SW, centred near S. Tide: Surf-Forecast mid and rising, Surf Atlas mid (too much water fattens it), Matosurf incoming to mid. SurferToday (unread) says medium to high. 'mid' is well supported. Size: Wikipedia 2-15 ft, and North Coast Watersports and Matosurf 'up to 15 ft', which supports the 15 ft max. The 3 ft min is close to Wikipedia's 2 ft. Matosurf's text largely repeats North Coast Watersports and Wikipedia, so the 15 ft figure has about two independent origins. Period: no numbers; Surf-Forecast says mostly groundswell. The 11/15 s profile values are unsupported. Season: Matosurf Oct-Mar, Surf Atlas 'much more common in the winter months' (encoded Dec-Feb), SurferToday (unread) Sep-May. All are inside or overlap the profile's Sep-Apr. Bathymetry: flat layers of Caithness flagstone (Wikipedia, Matosurf); Surf Atlas says slate shelf; World Beach Guide says a shallow, flat, kelp-covered reef. No survey data. Classification conflict: Surf-Forecast calls it a point break, while Wikipedia, Matosurf and World Beach Guide call it a reef. The only peer-reviewed item, McDowell 2025 (a history of surfing in Caithness), has an abstract with no wave conditions.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 2 ft (0.61 m) (scale not stated) | documented | S1 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | — | not documented | — | no separate setting; working range 3–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 15 ft (4.6 m) (scale not stated) | documented | S1, S5, S6, S7 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: Wikipedia says the reef holds swell from 2 feet (0.61 m), without stating whether this is face or offshore swell height.
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “The reef holds swell from 2 feet (0.61 m) upwards of 15 feet (4.6 m)”
- **Ideal range**: No excerpt states an ideal or best size range.
- **Maximum suitable**: Wikipedia says the reef holds swell upwards of 15 feet (4.6 m), North Coast Watersports and Matosurf (4.5 m) that it can handle or hold swell up to 15 ft, and World Beach Guide that it holds a big swell; no source states the scale.
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “The reef holds swell from 2 feet (0.61 m) upwards of 15 feet (4.6 m)”
  - S5 (North Coast Watersports): “When conditions align, it produces hollow, barreling waves and can handle swells up to 15 ft.”
  - S6 (Matosurf): “It can hold swell up to 15 feet (4.5 metres) and has hosted major contests”
  - S7 (World Beach Guide): “World class righthander breaking over a shallow, flat, kelp covered reef. Fast, hollow, powerful and holds a big swell”

  - S1 (Wikipedia): “The reef is made of layers of Caithness flagstone”
  - S6 (Matosurf): “A long, hollow, fast right-hander breaking over Caithness flagstone”
  - S4 (The Surf Atlas): “Break fast off a shelf of slate reef on the eastern side of the bay from Thurso town”
  - S7 (World Beach Guide): “breaking over a shallow, flat, kelp covered reef”
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast): “Take care to avoid the rocks.”

## Conflicting information

- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says offshore winds blow from the southeast and SurferToday's spec table lists SE, while SurferToday's text and Matosurf say a southerly offshore and Surf Atlas offshore S or SW winds.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast and Surf Atlas say mid tide and Matosurf incoming to mid, with Surf Atlas and Matosurf adding that too much water fattens it or takes its power, while SurferToday (search summary) says medium to high tide gives the best quality.
- **Geography · break type**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed point break, while Wikipedia, North Coast Watersports and World Beach Guide describe a reef and Matosurf a right-hander over flagstone; all that name a direction say right.
